Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.
  • According to recent reports, gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services.
  • The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

According to recent reports, gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

Recent findings suggest that in his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

Industry observers note that when you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”.

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

Sources indicate that “I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

Recent findings suggest that “So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

In a recent development, “Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”.

Leeds United forward Mateo Joseph has declared he is “focused on the comeback” as he plots a return to the pitch.

The 23-year-old succumbed to an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in March, while out on loan at Mallorca in La Liga.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He had requested a move away from Elland Road in the previous summer and scored two goals across 30 outings in Spain before being sidelined.

Joseph is now back on British shores, rehabilitating with the help of specialists at Leeds.

Posting on Instagram, the former Spain and England youth international remarked: “Back in Leeds, focused on the comeback.

“Every day brings progress, every step takes me closer, things are looking up and we’re moving in the right direction. One step at a time.”.

It is hard to envisage Joseph carving out a future at Leeds given the progress made by the club since his loan departure.

Whites boss Daniel Farke does not boast a wealth of forward options, yet Joseph would arguably find it tough to leapfrog Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha in the pecking order.

Speaking to The Yorkshire Post in the summer, Leeds icon Jermaine Beckford said: “Mateo has got talent. He's got technical ability. He's got good pace about him as well. We've seen when he's been with the under-21s how good he is at finishing.

Industry observers note that “He's had a couple of decent goals as well for the first team, I remember the Chelsea game at Stamford Bridge. He's got it, he just needs to knuckle down, get rid of the external noise, focus on working his socks off, and I think he could [force his way back in].

“Do I think Daniel Farke and the hierarchy want to keep him knowing that he could possibly upset the apple cart? I'm not entirely sure. But it's for Mateo to come back and show that this is a upcoming and improved version of himself. He's got the ability.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The dawn of the Mauricio Pochettino era is upon us, with the Argentine having taken to the dugout with the United States for the final time on Tuesday evening.

Pochettino is returning to the Premier League for a fourth time, replacing Michael Carrick as head coach of Manchester United.

He is facing a sizeable rescue mission, with Man United languishing in 18th in the Premier League having won just one of their first ten matches. He faces a tricky start, too, with Liverpool, Sporting CP, and Brentford on the docket for his first matches in charge.

While Carrick was formally dismissed last week, after the Man Utd hierarchy held crisis talks regarding his future in Monaco, Pochettino has been delayed in actually starting his new role.

He first had to see out one last international break with the United States national team, which involved a two-legged tie against Haiti, before returning to England.

Pochettino’s term as Manchester United manager will officially begin today, November 18, 2026, as confirmed in a club statement last week.

That start date was chosen to allow him to lead the United States national team through their two Concacaf Nations League matches this international break, a two-legged tie against Haiti. The second of those two legs kicked off at midnight on Tuesday night for UK viewers.

Industry observers note that the Argentine was set to travel to Manchester immediately after the match, on a private jet laid on by United. That will see him touch down in the north-west on Wednesday morning.

Pochettino is expected to head straight from the airport to Carrington, where he will throw himself headlong into preparing for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

Some of his backroom staff arrived on location in Manchester ahead of Pochettino, however, laying some groundwork before the head coach’s own arrival.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barnsley and Doncaster Rovers - down among the dead men in League One - will be hoping that rings true as they seek precious shafts of light following arduous autumns.

They face back-to-back derbies in their next two fixtures, which will assume importance not just for the morale of each club, but also for Daniel Stendel and Grant McCann in their second spells at the Reds and Rovers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sheffield Wednesday, Bradford City and Huddersfield Town have their own motivations to contend with.

Industry observers note that in the second half of last autumn, Barnsley slipped up at home to Rotherham United, who won in the league at Oakwell for the first time in 15 visits since March 1969. But they did afford themselves the fillip of three points at Doncaster 14 days later.

The Reds, who welcome the Owls on Friday before visiting Bradford - managed by ex-boss Michael Duff - next Tuesday, would probably settle for a 50 per cent derby ratio this time around.

More especially given that their grim winless league run - nine matches and counting - has descended into a crisis.

They must make do without top-scorer and suspended captain Cameron McGeehan on Friday, while defender Jack Shepherd, a boyhood Wednesdayite, is also banned. The return of Patrick Kelly from international duty with Northern Ireland is a much more welcome development.

The sight of in-form Owls striker and Reds old boy Davis Keillor-Dunn compounding their autumnal angst certainly wouldn't be.

A match-winning display from DKD - who has struck in his last three Wednesday matches - would put the tinlid on things for Reds followers, whose expectation levels are exceedingly low heading into Friday.

If things turn sour, the mood in the home stands has the potential to turn mutinous towards the club hierarchy. Barnsley are without a league win since September 2 and are only kept off the bottom of the table by goal difference. A protest from fans group Tykes Union is planned beforehand.

Derbies brought out the best in McCann's Rovers in League One last season and their recent 2-0 win over Wednesday keeping to that theme.

Rovers secured a derby double against arch-rivals Rotherham for the first time since 1949-50 and made history by winning league games at Barnsley and Millers in the same season.

McCann's side also beat Town and Bradford at home and performed very well in both away games and were extremely unlucky to lose both.

They visit the Bantams on Saturday, seeking to get back onside with supporters following dreadful away performances in their last two matches in league and cup - an embarrassing 3-0 FA Cup loss at non-league Kidderminster and an equally atrocious 6-1 league beating at MK Dons.

It has been revealed that on both occasions, McCann issued an apology to travelling fans with some starting to openly question his future. The Rovers chief, whose side host high-flying Town next Thursday, prides himself as being a fighter.

Wednesday’s derby form this term has been in keeping with their wretched numbers on that count over the past couple of years.

They have won just once in their past 14 league fixtures against White Rose counterparts.

So far this season, they were bullied in the second half of their meeting with Bradford in their opening home league fixture of 2026-27 - a 1-0 defeat which was more emphatic than the scoreline sounded.

By common consent, they were somewhat fortunate to secure a late point at Huddersfield on October 10 - when Town were very much the architects of their own downfall.

A fortnight later, a disjointed, unsatisfactory performance at Doncaster proved the final straw for the Owls hierarchy regarding Henrik Pedersen.

It has been revealed that historically, Oakwell at least provides rather happier memories for the Owls, notwithstanding their last visit. They have lost just once on their last eight trips up the A61.

After dismal displays - not just results - in three derby losses at Valley Parade, the Club Doncaster Sports Village and Oakwell last season, redressing the balance would be a barometer of Town’s progress in 26-27.

It’s a case of so far, so good with the Terriers avenging last season’s anaemic loss at Bradford with a cathartic victory on Hallowe’en. Statistically speaking, the visitors’ 3-0 triumph was their biggest ever at BD8.

In a recent development, they have two other scores to settle. Town were fitful in their 3-1 defeat at Oakwell last August and it was a sign of things to come for ex-head coach Lee Grant. They visit Barnsley on December 19.

There were jeers and opprobrium following a tepid 1-0 reverse in Doncaster on a February night when Town’s top-six pitch was exposed.

In a recent development, the present-day worries belong to Rovers. And Barnsley.

Verdict: Under 2.5 goals Best odds: 123/100 Bookmaker: 1xBet.

Arsenal resumes its title defense with a trip to Newcastle on Saturday, carrying a defensive record that gives Mikel Arteta every reason to approach another demanding away fixture with confidence. The champion has collected 27 points and seven clean sheets from its opening ten Premier League matches.

Newcastle has found consistency much harder to come by, although recent results suggest this could become a patient contest with relatively few goals.

According to recent reports, newcastle came close to entering the international break with a useful away victory. Jacob Murphy broke the deadlock at Fulham in the 80th minute, only for Rodrigo Muniz to equalize three minutes later. Harvey Barnes had also passed up a good opportunity, leaving Matthias Jaissle with some encouragement from the performance and frustration over the points that slipped away.

According to recent reports, that 1-1 draw followed a 2-0 league victory at Crystal Palace and a 1-0 home defeat against Everton. Each of those three matches finished below the 2.5-goal line, with Newcastle producing enough to remain competitive without consistently finding the finishing touch to settle games.

Against Arsenal, the balance between pressing and protecting midfield will matter. Newcastle’s best route appears to involve choosing its moments to attack, getting Barnes into space and making set pieces count. Giving the visitor repeated opportunities to attack an exposed back line would make an already difficult assignment considerably harder.

Joelinton remains an injury concern after missing the Fulham match, while goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen is unavailable with a hamstring problem. Jacob Ramsey’s one-match suspension applied to the Fulham fixture, leaving him eligible to return against Arsenal.

Arsenal has developed a useful habit of making a single goal sufficient. Its two most recent Premier League outings brought 1-0 victories over Liverpool and Hull City, with Martin Odegaard providing the breakthrough against Hull in the 72nd minute. That performance required patience, particularly while the visiting defense continued to frustrate Arsenal’s attempts to create clear chances.

In a recent development, the broader pattern strengthens the case for another restrained scoreline. Arsenal’s last four league victories have been achieved without conceding, beating Nottingham Forest, Everton, Liverpool and Hull while scoring five goals across those matches. Arteta’s side has been able to protect narrow advantages exceptionally well.

Sources indicate that for this trip, another controlled performance looks a reasonable expectation. Newcastle should provide a sterner physical examination than Hull, but Arsenal has already demonstrated at Anfield that it can leave a difficult ground with a clean sheet and three points.

Bukayo Saka remains sidelined, while Max Dowman is suspended. Martin Zubimendi needs assessment after suffering a muscle problem on international duty with Spain.

According to recent reports, william Saliba has taken another step toward returning by playing 45 minutes for the under-21 side. His involvement here remains a selection decision, rather than a confirmed return to the starting lineup.

Industry observers note that arsenal deserves favoritism, with its defensive discipline offering the strongest argument for another away victory. Newcastle should make the visitor work for opportunities, however, and the recent scoring patterns suggest this could remain close well into the second half.

Sources indicate that under 2.5 goals is the preferred selection. A 1-0 Arsenal victory is the predicted score, although a tight draw would also fit the reasoning behind the goals bet.

Verdict: Under 2.5 goals Best odds: 123/100 Bookmaker: 1xBet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

Industry observers note that the group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the eight teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position was Group A4 was confirmed after their win over Wales on Tuesday night, though it is Norway joining them in the knockout phases following a remarkable comeback win against Denmark.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

Sources indicate that the group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, Portugal.

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, Norway.

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

Industry observers note that it will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Recent findings suggest that toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

It has been revealed that still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

According to recent reports, at the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

According to recent reports, this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

In a recent development, “It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

Recent findings suggest that “The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

Industry observers note that “I love this energy [from the crowd]. Massive, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

Sources indicate that QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA.

According to recent reports, “It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”.

Substantial disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he stated he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Recent findings suggest that norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL.

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

It has been revealed that what about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one upcoming set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

Sources indicate that I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls).

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Sources indicate that verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv.

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin).

According to recent reports, mercedes have put a brand latest set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a massive moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x.

Recent findings suggest that the Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Sources indicate that verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen presently fastest inthe first sector.

In a recent development, the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Industry observers note that go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr.

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he notes Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

According to recent reports, it’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he remarked. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

Recent findings suggest that he added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

It has been revealed that the two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

According to recent reports, what about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Industry observers note that antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Industry observers note that most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

It has been revealed that not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change promptly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be key to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- newly introduced internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

In a recent development, hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have confirmed that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

In a recent development, aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who mentioned the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, mentioned the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti mentioned. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

In a recent development, “It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the significant upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

It has been revealed that almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

In a recent development, with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Industry observers note that formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car patch since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

In a recent development, this race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

Carl Ikeme has fondly recalled his loan spell at Middlesbrough - and believes anything but automatic promotion this season would be disappointing for the club.

The retired goalkeeper spent the entirety of his career on the books of Wolverhampton Wanderers, who loaned him out on nine separate occasions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He spent time at Middlesbrough during the 2011/12 season and made 10 appearances during the reign of Tony Mowbray.

A number of the 40-year-old’s former clubs are in the Championship promotion race, therefore it is something he is keeping a close eye on.

Industry observers note that “I think there’s some strong teams,” he told The Yorkshire Post. “I think out of the teams that were left in the Championship, they (Middlesbrough) were the standout team.

Industry observers note that “They nearly did it last year as well, they've probably learnt from that experience. They've got a great set-up at Boro as well, a really good club. It was one of my favourite loans, if not my favourite loan, great club, great set-up.

According to recent reports, “They've got a great owner as well and he's been there for a long time and he really takes his time and knows what he's doing. I'm not saying they're the team to beat but they've hit form quite soon. I think that obviously Wolves and West Ham will be there or thereabouts as well.

Recent findings suggest that “I think they'll be disappointed if they don't go up automatically this year but that being said, with Wolves, West Ham and Burnley coming down, it's going to be tough to get up for anyone. You've got the teams in and around the play-off picture, you've got the chasing pack as well.”.

Middlesbrough came within a whisker of promotion last term, losing to Hull City in the play-off final at Wembley.

Kim Hellberg’s side did not spend too long licking their wounds and sit second in the table after 15 games.

Sources indicate that “Out of the teams that were left in the Championship, they do look like the strongest,” Ikeme said. “I think Wolves will be hoping to kick on as the year goes on but Boro do look like one of the teams that will be in and around it.”.

Leeds United midfielder Sean Longstaff has conceded his move to Elland Road has not gone completely to strategy.

The 29-year-old signed for the Whites as part of their post-promotion recruitment drive in the summer of 2025, making a £12m move from his boyhood club Newcastle United.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He started his maiden campaign as a midfield regular but missed the weeks in which Leeds turned their season around through injury.

Opportunities were limited upon his return and competition in the middle of the park has only intensified in his second season.

He told The Official Leeds United Podcast: “I’d be lying if I remarked it’s been the easiest year I’ve ever had. It’s been a tough year.

“There’s probably been times, at home, especially, there’s times where you’re not that nice to be around. Ultimately, I made the decision to come to Leeds. I took my family away from the comforts of being at their home. I’ve took a newborn baby away from his grandparents to bring him down here for me to enhance my career.

Industry observers note that “Obviously, at the minute, it’s not gone probably to the perfect plan. But I don’t think life ever does.”.

Longstaff was handed his first league start of the season before the international break, completing 90 minutes in Leeds’ 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur.

He made his 200th Premier League appearance in the game and the reaching of the milestone in such a valuable win served as a reward for his perseverance.

It has been revealed that the midfielder said: “For me, I take training as serious as possible. Whether that’s the day after a game, whether it’s during the week, you’ve got to train as if you’re going to play.

Recent findings suggest that “And then ultimately, if you don’t play, that’s not in my control. I can’t control it. All I can control is, make sure I’m fit enough to play when I get a chance, make sure I’m sharp enough, make sure my mentality is right.

In a recent development, “If I get a chance, I want to try and show what I can do, whether that’s for 30 seconds whether that’s a for, come on at half-time, or whatever the case may be. I can’t control other people’s decisions. All I can control is the controllables.”.

Longstaff may not have seen the level of action he wanted in West Yorkshire, but has spoken of the club with great affection.

He has compared the Whites to Newcastle, who he made 214 appearances for before departing.

Industry observers note that he noted: “It’s still close to home so it didn’t feel like you were moving away miles. It’s not until you probably get down here, everyone indicates Leeds is a massive club, but until you get here, you don’t realise how big it is.

In a recent development, “I came with an expectation of ‘it’s going to be Newcastle’s this and Leeds is that’. Then you get in, you think ‘oh actually, Leeds is so similar.

“Apart from the kit, everything else felt exactly the same. Obviously the only difference is me being from Newcastle and not from Leeds, but actually got to know a lot of people from the city and they were telling us stuff. The way they speak about Leeds is the way I felt about Newcastle. The more you meet people, the more you realise it’s massive.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has said to “give him time” to make Manchester United the dominant club in the city again as he prepares to start work.

Pochettino will take charge of Man United for the first time against Liverpool on Sunday after being appointed to succeed Michael Carrick, who was sacked last week with the club sitting 18th in the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s return to club management has been delayed after being allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States national team.

His last game ended in a 2-0 win for USA against Haiti in Cincinnati during the early hours on Wednesday (UK time) to wrap up an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

AC Milan forward Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a spectacular overhead kick and teenager Julian Hall doubled the hosts’ lead before half-time.

After bidding an emotional farewell to the USA supporters inside the stadium, Pochettino immediately turned his attentions to the task at hand with Man United and the rivalry with Manchester City.

According to recent reports, told by former Man City loanee DaMarcus Beasley that “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue” in the TNT Sports US studio after the game, Pochettino responded: “You will see. Give me time.

“The upcoming challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenalin you want to feel.

“We need to add our common sense… we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing.”.

Pochettino heads to Old Trafford tasked with steering Man United out of the relegation zone before he can target winning titles and eventually usurping Man City as the dominant team in the city.

United have not been crowned Premier League champions since Sir Alex Ferguson retired, with the legendary Scotsman final season being the last time the club finished above their neighbours in the table.

Additional reporting by Press Association.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 13:16 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 13 November 2026.

Egypt will begin their African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches with a upcoming manager after their previous head coach was sacked amid a torrid breakdown of both of his marriages.

Hossam Hassan was handed his marching orders on Saturday after an incident in August which saw his two wives embroiled in a vicious fight, captured and shared on social media.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel bar in the upscale Porto Marina resort on Egypt's north coast.

El-Gharbawy and Mustafa were videoed arguing with Hassan in the middle attempting to cool tensions, but the duo came to blows, with punches thrown and hair pulled as screams filled the air.

Such was the stress of the incident that Hassan is believed to have fainted as he tried to separate the two women.

Horrified public onlookers watched as the physical fight grew with relatives of the trio getting involved, and security was called before Hassan was taken to hospital.

Industry observers note that en Égypte, un violent différend a éclaté entre... les deux femmes du sélectionneur égyptien, Hossam Hassan. 🇪🇬😳Le conflit a dégénéré en échauffourée avec coups et tirage de cheveux, avant que des jeunes et des passages n'interviennent dans la bagarre. pic.twitter.com/pvRUSMtAsD.

Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan was sacked this week after a fight broke out between his two wives.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel in the upscale Porto Marina resort.

The 60-year-old is believed to have fainted while trying to separate the two women.

Both women are believed to have been left with cuts and bruises following the vicious scrap, while Hassan, despite briefly losing consciousness, was left unharmed.

His lawyers later told Sky News Arabia, via the Sun, that he was not suffering a health crisis during the incident, and that he remained in good health.

But in the days that followed, Hassan started proceedings to divorce El-Gharbawy, who he has been married to for decades. The couple also share three children.

The 60-year-old has a further two children with second wife Mustafa, who Le Parisien alleges also filed for divorce in the days after the footage went viral on social media.

The Egyptian Football Association ensured that Hassan's professional life took a similar nosedive, sharing in a statement that his dismissal was due in part to reputational damage the scandal might be doing to the national team.

'After analysing all the circumstances and events of the past few days, as well as their consequences and the negative impact they have had on the positive image and stability of our national team, the Board of Directors has decided, within the framework of its responsibilities, to dismiss coach Hossam Hassan and his entire technical staff and to end his tenure,' their statement read.

Mustafa's lawyer Mohamed Shams gave an interview on Sky News Arabia claiming that his client had been the victim of a 'premeditated attack'.

'We hoped it wouldn't come to divorce, but things escalated to this level.'.

Hassan married his second wife in 2015, with Egyptian law allowing Muslim men to marry up to four women, providing that any wives have been formally informed that another marriage is to take place.

The law mandates that the husband is also obligated to treat all of his wives equally with regard to housing, financial support and standard of living.

Hassan had been married to his first wife El-Gharbawy for decades, with the pair sharing three of his five children.

Hassan and Mustafa briefly separated four years ago before recoupling before the spat that ended both of his marriages.

As well as being relieved of his duties, Hassan was also sanctioned by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation, leaving him unable to publicly address the media following his sacking.

Mohamed Salah and Co will now play their first qualifier of the international break against Malawi under fresh head coach Ali Maher.

The former Liverpool star could be among those Pharaohs stars privately pleased with the departure of Hassan, after he was benched by his ex-manager for the last two international clashes.

When asked why the superstar and national team captain had been left on the sidelines for the ties, Hassan had said: 'It is not right for a country of 120 million people for the national team to depend on one player.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United is officially underway, and his first game is just days away.

The Red Devils return from the final international break of 2026 to face the daunting prospect of visiting arch-rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend.

Pochettino inherits a side with just one win in 10 top-flight games this term, a string of results that have left Man Utd in the relegation zone.

The Argentine’s style of play centres around a high-press and an ability to build from the back - two things United have struggled with so far this season.

Injuries across the pitch will impact Pochettino’s selection, with Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko definitely ruled out for the trip to Anfield.

In goal, Senne Lammens is established first-choice and that is unlikely to change with Pochettino’s arrival, while the Argentine might be tempted to copy Michael Carrick and play Leny Yoro at right-back, instructing the Frenchman to tuck in and form a three-man defence in possession.

However, Diogo Dalot will likely start at right-back, with a much more simple defensive approach.

Yoro could therefore partner Ayden Heaven in the heart of defence to give United a bit more pace than a backline featuring Harry Maguire, but the experience of Lisandro Martinez may be hard to ignore as Pochettino balances a squad lacking in confidence.

Patrick Dorgu is a doubt after being sent home from international duty with Denmark, but is stated to be winning his battle to be fit for the Anfield trip and could replicate what Antonee Robinson did for Pochettino at left-back.

With the USA, Pochettino had settled on a 4-3-3 formation, with the midfield featuring a sitting player behind two more proactive team-mates.

Industry observers note that pochettino’s immediate issue with the Man United squad will be the fact that there is no clear candidate as a holding midfielder. The injured Baleba does well at screening the backline, but his strengths rely on driving forward with the ball.

The deep-lying playmaker role is a battle between Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. Pochettino has shown a tendency to trust young, talented players, so it would not be a surprise to see the former Tottenham manager try and work his magic with Mainoo.

Tielemans could play the box-to-box role alongside Mainoo, offering experience during the transition to Pochettino’s ideal approach.

While Pochettino has utilised a deeper player in the middle of the park with the USA, it is likely that he will instead have to build a more attacking midfield at United.

That is because club captain Bruno Fernandes is clearly the Red Devils’ best player, which merits his inclusion.

Matheus Cunha looks a good fit on the left wing as a creative spark, while Bryan Mbeumo’s pace down the right wing would allow Pochettino to create a similar attacking shape to his USA side.

However, with United’s striking options limited, it would not be a surprise to see Mbeumo lead the line, with Amad Diallo playing instead on the right.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have turned to Mauricio Pochettino as their upcoming manager, and a new backroom staff will be joining him for his return to the Premier League.

After identifying ex-Tottenham boss Pochettino as the desired replacement for sacked head coach Michael Carrick, Man Utd promptly agreed personal terms - before approaching the USA to extract their target from a four-year contract only signed following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

It has been reported that the total compensation package United will have to pay the US Soccer Federation could be north of £10million, once fees for Pochettino’s staff have been included.

Assistant manager Jesus Perez has worked with Pochettino since his first job in management, employed initially as an analyst at Espanyol in LaLiga.

After building a strong relationship with Pochettino, Spaniard Perez was promoted to No2 when the Argentine was appointed manager of Southampton in 2013, and has been his assistant at every job since.

Perez and Pochettino joked about the United job during the World Cup, with the former apparently very keen on working at Old Trafford.

There are four other members of staff likely to make the move across the Atlantic.

Miguel D’Agostino is a former team-mate of Pochettino’s, with the duo having played together at Newell’s Old Boys in their native Argentina.

Initially working as a scout for Pochettino at Espanyol, D’Agostino has also followed his compatriot from club to club since then.

Sources indicate that toni Jimenez is another to have worked with Pochettino at every club he has managed so far, plus the US national team. A goalkeeping coach, Jimenez first linked up with Pochettino in 2011 at Espanyol.

Thomas Tuchel’s side scored three goals in 12 minutes either side of half-time to stun Spain before withstanding a late siege to seal their finest win under the German boss.

Harry Kane took his international tally to 93 goals with a penalty on the stroke of half-time as England deservedly ended the opening 45 minutes ahead.

England fans feared a collapse similar to the one the team suffered in last summer’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second with 20 minutes remaining.

But this time England kept their opponents at bay with some resolute defending and two superb saves from goalkeeper James Trafford.

Rice was full of praise for his teammates after the Nations League win and said he ‘knew’ England would beat the world champions in their own backyard.

In a recent development, ‘Our first ten minutes were probably the best we’ve played. It was pressure, pressure, pressure – we could have had two or three.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.
  • England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.
  • The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage.

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente stated when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that ‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’.

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’.

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the key tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’.

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’.

Bruno Fernandes has rejected a latest contract at Manchester United against the turbulent backdrop of the departure of head coach Michael Carrick.

The Manchester United captain publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Discussions are believed to have started between Fernandes and Man United over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But after an initial proposal from the club is thought to have been rejected by the midfield talisman, Fernandes has now snubbed a second deal with improved terms, in what could be an early headache for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The Portuguese international's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract, but will continue talks over aspects including his salary and the length of his new deal as they are keen for him to stay.

Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second set of terms from Manchester United as the club seeks to pin him down to a upcoming deal.

The club captain inked his latest terms in 2024 with his contract set to expire next June.

Man United currently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season, and announcing a newly introduced deal for Fernandes might have given the club an vital boost of morale during a difficult international break.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he claims in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he noted.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'.

Industry observers note that his post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

It has been revealed that 'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he noted. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Fernandes was publicly critical of his former head coach Michael Carrick last month but was later adamant that he had not held clear-the-air talks with him.

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

In a recent development, 'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'.

Fernandes' sabre-rattling was ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on Thursday after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco earlier this week to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Thursday evening that staff members inside the club have been upset with the protracted sacking, which has been deemed disrespectful of Carrick's status as a club legend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charlton manager Nathan Jones is among a number of head coaches in English football’s top four divisions to have objected to the reduction in how many yellow cards leads to a touchline ban.

Standard Sport understands that at a recent managers’ meeting, Jones and other head coaches from clubs among the 92 argued a 2023 change in FA rules towards stricter punishments for technical-area misconduct remains unjustified at a time when football managers have never faced greater pressure and volatility.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is incongruous with an increasingly demanding working environment.

Head coaches across the Premier League and EFL are understood to have this season been shown research that suggests managers’ behaviour usually improves once they reach three bookings.

Managers are regularly reminded of a variety of regulations including technical-area misconduct rules during meetings with the FA’s disciplinary teams, who often present research and statistics to contextualise changes to rules or emerging trends.

Ahead of the 2018-19 season, new rules were introduced to clean up touchline behaviour. Managers across the FA Cup, EFL, Carabao Cup, EFL Trophy and National League could receive yellow and red cards for the first time, with four yellows resulting in a one-match touchline ban.
