📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Sources indicate that carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

It has been revealed that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager noted. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

Industry observers note that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Recent findings suggest that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and swiftly.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick mentioned: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

Recent findings suggest that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

In a recent development, 3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu.

Sources indicate that the Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

Sources indicate that “We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

In a recent development, “We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

According to recent reports, “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

More jeers at the final whistle from United fans - they weren’t happy with this point against a team there for the taking after Rodrigo Bentancur’s dismissal. Michael Carrick is still trying to find answers because this United team is not clicking.

The late chaos is over at Old Trafford as Solanke rescues a precious point for Tottenham with that 92nd minute equaliser. Man Utd thought they had the game wrapped up after Mbeumo’s well-taken opener was followed by Bentancur’s crazy red card. However, Spurs, who were the better team throughout the contest, kept fighting and found a fully deserved leveller. The visitors remain winless, but it’s another worrying performance from Carrick’s side, who have picked up just one victory in six top-flight matches.

Incredible drama at Old Trafford! Tonali floats a cross into the box and Solanke shrugs off Martinez, before flicking a delicate header into the bottom corner to send Spurs’ away support wild. Man Utd are stunned. Could the visitors go on and win this now?

You can feel the nervousness in the Old Trafford crowd. Spurs’ dominance has calmed over the last 10 minutes, but Man Utd have failed to take control or pick up the tempo.

This game looks it could be time for Baleba’s much-anticipated debut. Man Utd’s current midfield doesn’t possess enough running power and Tottenham are exploiting that.

Man Utd’s slow start prompts some boos from the home fans. Cunha attempts to rally the crowd, but his side have given their supporters nothing to be positive about in this game so far. From a Spurs perspective, you can see why they’ve only scored two top-flights goals this season. They should be two-nil up, but they’ve notably lacked end-product.

Michael Carrick has made two changes to the side which drew against Fulham. Amad Diallo returns to the fold after a spell on the sidelines with an injury, replacing Marcus Rashford, who drops to the bench. The other alteration comes in defence, with Diogo Dalot departing for Leny Yoro.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

According to recent reports, the strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

Recent findings suggest that the spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after substantial-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

Recent findings suggest that all eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 16:37.

Liverpool are reportedly showing a keen interest in signing Brazilian youngster Arthur Dias.

Dias has graduated from Athletico Paranaense's youth system and has made 55 senior appearances since breaking into the first team last year.

The 19-year-old has featured 37 times during the current season, and his impressive performances have attracted the attention of Liverpool and several other heavyweight clubs.

Tottenham Hotspur reportedly made an attempt to sign Dias during the summer transfer window, submitting an offer worth around £16.6m, but their pursuit proved unsuccessful.

According to a report from Fussballeuropa, Spurs retain their interest alongside Liverpool, although Athletico-PR could demand a fee in the region of £25m for their prized asset.

Liverpool have sent scouts to watch him in recent matches as they continue to monitor the highly rated youngster's progress.

Aside from the two Premier League clubs, La Liga champions Barcelona are also in the race and have reportedly scouted him on several occasions.

There is also considerable interest from Germany, with Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig understood to be weighing up moves for the defender in January.

The Reds should be looking to recruit a fresh centre-back next summer, with Joe Gomez potentially heading for the exit door.

With Virgil van Dijk still performing at a high level, Andoni Iraola could look to bring in more young defensive talent and gradually develop them into potential successors to the Dutchman.

Liverpool have also been linked with a move for former defender Jarell Quansah, although it would likely take a substantial offer to bring him back to Anfield.

There is little harm in building a pool of exciting young defenders at the club, but whether Liverpool would be prepared to pay £25m for Dias remains to be seen.

In the summer, Virgil van Dijk was a distant dream for AC Milan, but their chances of signing him next year are on the rise.

Barcelona have released a statement confirming that Pau Cubarsi picked up an injury during Spain's UEFA Nations League contest with England on Sunday night.

Cubarsi started the clash with the Three Lions but was substituted at the half-time break.

Barcelona have revealed that the centre-back has strained his hip flexor, but it is unclear at this stage of proceedings how long the 19-year-old could be on the sidelines.

“First-team player Pau Cubarsi has ​​a strain in his iliopsoas muscle. His availability for the match against Villarreal will depend on his recovery," read a statement from Barcelona.

Cubarsi has not yet been ruled out of Barcelona's La Liga clash with Villarreal on Sunday, but he is a doubt at this stage of proceedings.

The defender has been a vital player for Barcelona during the 2026-27 campaign, making 13 appearances in all competitions, providing two assists in the process.

Cubarsi will now not be in action with Spain until March, when the Nations League quarter-finals take place, with his full focus in the months ahead therefore set to be on Barcelona.

After the clash with Villarreal, Barcelona will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with an away fixture against Sabah on November 25.

Barcelona will then finish the move away to Deportivo La Coruna in La Liga, before beginning December with a clash against Atletico Madrid on December 2.

Hansi Flick's side beat Atletico 2-1 when the pair last met on November 8.

Jules Kounde remains on the sidelines through injury, and he is unlikely to be unavailable for the clash against Villarreal this weekend.

However, Eric Garcia made his return from a muscular injury against Atletico as a second-half substitute, and the Spain international will likely replace Cubarsi in the starting side against Villarreal, should the latter be unavailable for selection.

Why, therefore, would he have expected cap No102 to be any different?

This was meant to have been a celebration of one of Scotland’s greatest-ever servants on the night when he equalled Kenny Dalglish’s total appearances against the whipping boys of Nations League Group B1.

As the cliché goes, there’s no gimmes at this level. But that’s nonsense. This is exactly what Robertson’s special night should have been. A gimme.

The problem is that Scotland weren’t much better. In the first half, at least.

Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps as Scotland saw off North Macedonia.

Thankfully, they got the job done after the break to ensure it would be a night Robertson will look back on fondly after all.

Recent findings suggest that he’s earned that too, even if his own individual performance didn’t quite hit the heights of so many that have gone before. But nobody will remember that.

In a recent development, perhaps he knackered himself by covering what must have been around 10km in a small-sided kickabout during the warm-up. He may not have the same turn of pace in his arsenal that he possessed when he first broke into the international fold as a fresh-faced teenager. But, in terms of intensity, the 32-year-old is still an animal, in the nicest possible way. He hassled and harried every one of his team-mates throughout the pre-game stuff, barking out all sorts of instructions along the way.

In a recent development, in many ways, he is still the same standard-bearer he’s always been. It was a shame he couldn’t quite lead the way when the serious stuff got started.

According to recent reports, operating on the left-hand side of a four-man midfield, the Spurs man – as he does as frequently as ever – bombed up and down the flank all night. However, his deliveries from several promising positions weren’t quite up to scratch.

A couple hit the first man. A couple cleared the upright. None caused any sort of alarm in the North Macedonian backline.

Robertson was his customary energetic self as he bombed up and down the left-hand side.

He was made to work harder than he would have liked at the other end too, as the visitors threatened to spoil the party on more than one occasion in the second 45.

Recent findings suggest that in truth, he didn’t look particularly comfortable in Sebastien Pocognoli’s new-look side. Then again, few did.

Recent findings suggest that the Belgian will be given plenty of time to really put his stamp on this Scotland team, but there’s no two ways about it. The early signs are uninspiring to say the least.

By the end, people got sick of the attritional style employed by Steve Clarke. Pocognoli arrived with a reputation for going with a more enterprising approach.

It has been revealed that really? It’s fair to say, the wait to see it in action goes on.

In a recent development, it’s not the time to panic. But you get the sense patience is already being stretched amongst some sections of the Tartan Army.

They weren’t shy in airing their frustrations last night. Scott McTominay was on the receiving end of a few grumbles, as was Ben Gannon-Doak who once again did so much right until the all-vital crucial last bit.

Yes, he may have won the winning penalty which John McGinn duly slotted away, but let’s be honest, there was more than a touch of good fortune about it.

The Scotland skipper leads his side out at Hampden on a night he will remember forever.

He should have burst the net when put clean through by Oli McBurnie long before keeper Stole Dimitrievski caught him near the byline.

Industry observers note that the Bournemouth youngster is seen by many as undroppable, and there’s merit to that argument in that Pocognoli doesn’t have anyone else like him to call upon. However, he needs to improve the final part of his game to ensure he becomes Scotland’s main man in the years to come.

Had Scotland been a few goals to the good by the time McGinn stepped up to notch his second of the night, you suspect Robertson may have fancied taking the spot-kick himself.

If only it had been that comfortable.

Still, the record books will show that Robertson’s record-equalling night will ultimately go down as a triumph for all involved, even if it didn’t feel like it at the time.

Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For over a decade, scientists have warned the world must limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) to avoid the most severe consequences of climate change.
  • Decades of "insufficient" action on cutting the fossil fuel emissions heating the planet means overshooting 1.5-degree temperature threshold is now "imminent and unavoidable," according to the United Nations Environment Program's (UNEP) annual Emissions Gap Report.
  • If current climate policies continue, temperatures will rise by an average of 2.8 degrees Celsius (5 Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels within this century.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For over a decade, scientists have warned the world must limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) to avoid the most severe consequences of climate change.

That goal is no longer within reach.

Decades of "insufficient" action on cutting the fossil fuel emissions heating the planet means overshooting 1.5-degree temperature threshold is now "imminent and unavoidable," according to the United Nations Environment Program's (UNEP) annual Emissions Gap Report.

If current climate policies continue, temperatures will rise by an average of 2.8 degrees Celsius (5 Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels within this century. But even if countries meet their new climate pledges, global warming is still projected to reach 2.6 degrees Celsius. Both scenarios would tip the world into a period of catastrophic weather extremes.

The projections reflect a gap between what governments promise to do and the action they are taking to curb emissions. Some 167 countries have submitted climate action plans to the UN, covering 83% of global greenhouse gas emissions. But those pledges to cut emissions fall far short of what is needed to limit warming.

Among the world's largest emitters, Indonesia, China and the United States saw emissions rise in 2025, according to preliminary estimates. The increase in the US "far exceeded that of all other countries," driven by a resurgence of coal — the dirtiest fossil fuel source — and rising electricity demand, partly linked to massive AI data center expansion.

Recent findings suggest that the outlook has worsened in part because of US President Donald Trump's withdrawal of the United States from the historic Paris climate accord in which the world came together in 2015 to agree to halt climate change. The US is the second-largest annual emitter of climate-warping greenhouse gases.

Since Trump entered the Oval Office for a second time in January 2025, his administration has taken a sledgehammer to climate policy, gutting environmental regulations and expanding oil and gas production.

"The main takeaway is simple — governments need to get on with enacting policies that cut fossil fuel use as soon as possible," mentioned Bill Hare, CEO of the global science and policy institute Climate Analytics, of the report.

Exceeding 1.5 degrees Celsius even temporarily sets humanity on a dangerous course, as it increases the risk of triggering potentially irreversible or difficult-to-undo "tipping points," like the loss of coral reefs, long-term retreat of ice sheets, and the Amazon rainforest— a key carbon sink — turning into a grassland.

As ecosystems disappear and sea levels rise, these changes could trigger a deadly chain reaction, releasing more greenhouse gases and accelerating warming, dramatically increasing the likelihood of deadly extreme weather.

This summer alone, Europe recorded more than 32,000 excess deaths related to heat and nearly 1,500 people died in a flash floods in Nepal and Tibet, after climate change laid the groundwork for a glacier to collapse.

It has been revealed that but scientists maintain 1.5 degrees Celsius is not a magic number, and that every fraction of a degree of warming brings escalating risks. To reduce the risk of future damage, countries should still focus on rapidly transitioning away from fossil fuels, the largest contributor to global climate change, and toward renewable energy like solar and wind.

Now the best-case scenario is overshooting 1.5 degrees Celsius for a short time before bringing temperatures back down quickly.

Industry observers note that "Overshoot is not surrender," UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres mentioned in a press statement in late October. "We can still keep it as small and as short as possible — and bring temperatures back below 1.5 degrees before the end of the century.".

UNEP lays out a scenario in which the world sees warming peak at 1.7 to 1.8 degrees Celsius around mid-century, before falling back to 1.5 Celsius by 2100. Getting there would require steep emissions cuts of 69% by 2040, relative to 2025 levels.

It would also require removing 330 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it in the ground. But recent studies have cast doubt on the feasibility and costs of the technology, as well as the ability of the nascent carbon removal industry to scale as quickly as required to meet climate goals.

The UN has warned that any delays will make the challenge harder, saying that every five years that emissions remain at current levels adds about 0.1 Celsius to projected peak warming.

According to recent reports, "We must pull out all the stops to minimize peak warming and return to 1.5 Celsius by the end of the century," Inger Andersen, executive director of UNEP, said in a press release. "This is possible.".

Recent findings suggest that still, climate policies have proven effective in reducing emissions. The UNEP report draws on more than 200 studies that analyze how measures like carbon taxes, government climate targets, building codes and subsidies for low-carbon technologies are working.

Recent findings suggest that carbon-pricing schemes have been the most widely studied so far. China's pilot schemes reduced emissions by about 11%, while the European Union's emissions trading system saw an 8% cut, compared with projected levels without these policies.

"There are more opportunities than ever to accelerate action," according to the report, pointing to the boom in renewable energy since the adoption of the Paris Agreement a decade ago.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that global renewable electricity capacity has grown three times faster than anticipated, and solar build-out grew seven times faster. In 2024, more than 90% of renewable projects were cheaper than fossil fuel alternatives.

Industry observers note that while total energy supply from coal, oil and gas has continued to rise, that's happened at a slower rate than was projected in 2015. And coal use is likely to peak and decline by the end of the decade.

"We have a wealth of success stories showing that emissions can be cut swiftly," Andersen noted. "It is now up to nations to urgently put in place policies that spark fast, deep and sustained emissions reductions, and put the world on track for a more stable climate and more stable economies and societies.".

  • Sources indicate that A re-evaluation of data from the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has corroborated the findings that yielded the first-ever photo of a black hole.
  • The funding that voters in California have approved to earmark for immunology research — the largest ever infusion of cash for science authorized by a public vote in US history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physicists used an algorithm to combine telescope measurements of a black hole in a different way from the original analysis.Credit: S. Lai, N. Thyagarajan, O. I. Wong and F. Diakogiannis/CSIRO.

Sources indicate that A re-evaluation of data from the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has corroborated the findings that yielded the first-ever photo of a black hole. After the blurry image was released in 2019, sceptics argued that the circular shape seen in the shot was an artefact of the team’s image-reconstruction techniques. Independent astrophysicist Samuel Lai and his team used different methods to reanalyse the original data and their results — including new images of the black hole — largely match those of the EHT team.

The funding that voters in California have approved to earmark for immunology research — the largest ever infusion of cash for science authorized by a public vote in US history. (Nature | 5 min read).

Recent findings suggest that researchers have catalogued almost 100 proteins that get a free pass through the blood–brain barrier to maintain the health of neurons. Most of these proteins were produced in distant organs, particularly the liver. The team found that the transport of some of these proteins is disrupted in mice with a brain disease that mimics early-stage Alzheimer’s disease. The work suggests that the brain actively imports the proteins it needs to stay healthy, and that the breakdown of that transport drives the dysfunction seen in neurodegenerative disease, claims neuroscientist and study co-author Andrew Yang.

The launch of the Artemis II mission to orbit the Moon produced unprecedented large-scale atmospheric disturbances, say researchers. Data from GPS receivers found that the Space Launch System — the most powerful rocket that NASA has ever built — disrupted the atmospheric layer known as the ionosphere. The GPS disruption was potentially large enough to “have a strong impact not only on self-driving cars but also on drone positioning,” says space physicist and study co-author Charles Lin.

Reference: Geophysical Research Letters preprint (not peer reviewed).

The scientific literature contains decades-old papers that detail fraudulent, unethical or merely incorrect results, but aren’t marked as such. Many of these papers are long neglected, but their digitization enables artificial-intelligence tools that summarize scientific literature on a topic to feed misinformation to a new generation. This leaves publishers to wrangle with the question of whether these historical papers should be retracted or flagged as suspect — a task that can be tricky if authors are dead, original records can’t be consulted or journals are no longer in print.

According to recent reports, “You need a container before you can get the chemistry” that enables cellular life, claims astrobiologist Bruce Damer. He’s among those researchers who favour a ‘lipid-first’ hypothesis for the origin of complex life: that the lipid membrane that corrals the cell is key to its success. Or even that bubbles of lipids, plus the chemistry they enclosed, could have propagated and evolved in a Darwinian-like way, before RNA (or DNA) arrived on the scene.

Enjoy more ideas about where we came from in Quanta Magazine’s Origins of Life Week.

Social scientists should be involved in the process of finding suitable locations for fresh observatories, argues anthropologist Jaco de Swart, co-principal investigator of a proposed neutrino detector to be built in the Peruvian Andes. Many suitable locations for such projects are sensitive ecological environments with cultural significance for Indigenous communities. Social scientists can help to integrate environmental care into these projects and build relationships with local and Indigenous stakeholders. “To build scientific infrastructure that is responsible, just and resilient, humanities scholars must have leadership roles from the start,” de Swart writes.

Appearing in the Jurassic Park franchise is the strongest predictor of a dinosaur species’ popularity, according to new research — an example of the ‘blockbuster effect’. The media should leverage this effect to put a spotlight on endangered species, says zoologist Pâmela Lima. (Science | 7 min read).

Reference: Biology Letters paper.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03675-y.

The Kangaroo is a multiple-choice mathematics challenge attempted by more than seven million children in around 120 countries, just for fun. By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 16 Nov 2026 17:16.

Copa Sudamericana hopefuls Vasco da Gama will be looking to move into the top half of the Brasileirao table when they welcome relegation-threatened Internacional to Estadio Sao Januario this midweek.

The hosts sit 11th with 44 points after 34 matches, below 10th-placed Sao Paulo on goal difference, while the visitors are 16th on 38 points, just one point above the drop zone, making this an important meeting for both sides.

Although Vasco have enjoyed a marginally better second half of the campaign compared to their first 19 league outings (W5, D5, L9), the Gigante da Colina only recently recorded their first back-to-back top-flight wins since enjoying three straight victories between mid-September and early October.

Pedro Emanuel's side came from behind to beat Atletico-PR 3-1 in Curitiba on November 4 before travelling to Arena Conda and securing a 2-0 victory over Chapecoense 10 days later, courtesy of Bruno Duarte.

Both results came either side of a Copa do Brasil semi-final exit at the hands of Palmeiras following a penalty loss after a 2-2 aggregate draw, although there is no getting away from the fact that Emanuel has overseen an impressive improvement since taking charge in July.

However, the Portuguese coach must find a better balance at both ends of the pitch with time running out, as his side have scored 45 goals and conceded 50 in the league this season, while an improvement at Sao Januario is also needed.

Vasco have won just one of their last three league home games (D1, L1), with their most recent outing ending in a 4-1 defeat to leaders Flamengo, although Wednesday's hosts have picked up a decent 27 points from 17 top-flight matches on home soil this season.

Internacional head into this encounter on the back of a dramatic 1-0 victory over Coritiba, courtesy of an Alerrandro stoppage-time penalty, a result that lifted the team from southern Brazil out of the relegation zone.

Eduardo Baptista's side have now won nine of their 34 league matches (D11, L14) this season, scoring 38 goals and conceding 42, while alternating between defeats and victories across their most recent four outings.

Chasing their first consecutive Brasileirao victories since back-to-back wins against Santos and Chapecoense in March, the Colorado must also contend with a poor away record that has seen them pick up just 15 points from an available 51 on the road this season while failing to take maximum points in any of their last four trips (D1, L3).

However, having recorded victories in six of their last nine matches against Vasco (D1, L2), including a 4-1 success in the reverse fixture, Inter should have some reason for optimism heading into this encounter.

Three of those triumphs have come in four of their last four visits to Sao Januario, although the Colorado suffered a 5-1 defeat on their most recent trip to the ground.

Vasco da Gama form (all competitions):.

Internacional form (all competitions):.

Vasco could again be without Thiago Mendes, Nuno Moreira, Santiago Sosa and Tche Tche, all of whom missed the recent victory over Chapecoense through fitness problems.

Cauan Barros and Carlos Cuesta have also been sidelined with injuries in recent weeks, while Robert Renan is a doubt after being substituted in the 60th minute last time out due to physical discomfort.

Andre Gomez is joint-top scorer for the hosts with five league goals this season, alongside the injured Mendes, and the former heads into this encounter in good spirits after providing an assist in the previous outing.

Meanwhile, Duarte, who was the hero in that game, is expected to lead the line once again as he looks to add to his four top-flight goals this season.

As for Inter, defender Guillermo Maripan will play no part after receiving a red card while on the bench in stoppage time during their last outing.

On the injury front, Alan Patrick (muscle), Antonio Sanabria (calf), Kayky (ankle), Sergio Rochet (back), Matheus Cunha (elbow), Anthoni (knee) and Benjamin Arhin (hamstring) are also sidelined for this encounter.

Vasco da Gama possible starting lineup:.

Leandro; Rodriguez, Saldivia, Renan, Piton; Jair; Hinestroza, Lescano, Gomez, Colidio; Duarte.

Internacional possible starting lineup:.

Santos Oliveira; Gomes, Mercado, Juninho; Aguirre, Villagra, Maia, Bahia; Carbonero, Vitinho; Alerrandro.

Vasco's recent results and home advantage make them difficult to oppose, particularly against an Internacional side that has struggled badly on its travels, so we are backing the hosts to claim victory here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 17:20, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 17:40.

Crystal Palace have declared the appointment of Thomas Frank as their upcoming head coach.

The 53-year-old arrives at Selhurst Park following the departure of predecessor Pierre Sage, who was sacked last Thursday after less than five months in charge.

Frank has put pen to paper on a contract that runs through to June 2029 and returns to management for the first time since he was dismissed by Tottenham Hotspur in February.

According to recent reports, "It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it,” Frank told Crystal Palace’s official website.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.”.

Sources indicate that chairman Steve Parish added: “I’m delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace. He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

“I’m confident Thomas’ extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season.”.

It has been revealed that we are pleased to confirm the appointment of Thomas Frank as Manager ? ℹ️ https://t.co/2wUzZAGt4S https://t.co/zv2vMPGPFz.

Over the summer, Frank opened up about using his break from management to his advantage before making the next step in his career.

Sources indicate that "Football remains a huge part of who I am, and I have chosen to use this time productively. Over the coming months, besides spending time with family and friends, I will continue studying, observing and learning from other leaders both within sport and beyond it.

“Time away from the touchline is allowing me to broaden my perspective and gather insights that I look forward to bringing into my next challenge.

"When the time is right, I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication.”.

That time is now with Crystal Palace, with Frank becoming the third manager to take charge of three different London clubs in the Premier League after Alan Pardew (Charlton, Crystal Palace, West Ham) and Harry Redknapp (QPR, Spurs, West Ham).

At Spurs, Frank won just 13 of his 38 games and left the club sitting down in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

Before his brief spell in North London, Frank made his name as a first-team manager with Brentford where he enjoyed a successful seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025.

Frank guided the Bees to the Premier League after winning promotion from the Championship in 2020-21, and he established them as a competitive top-flight team that finished 13th, ninth, 16th and 10th across the following four campaigns, accumulating more than 50 points in three of those.

Across spells with Brentford and Spurs, Frank has won 61, drawn 46 and lost 71 of his 178 Premier League games as a manager (34.27% win ratio).

He is now tasked with steering upcoming club Crystal Palace away from the relegation picture as the Eagles bid to shake off a disappointing start to the campaign and extend their 13-year stay in the Premier League.

Palace at the moment sit rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their first 10 games under Sage, but they could move out of the bottom three and up to 16th place if Frank wins his first game in charge away against Coventry City on Saturday.

Frank has plenty of rebuilding to do at Selhurst Park, with three key priorities sitting at the top of his in-tray.

The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered.
  • How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.
  • It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Sources indicate that their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In a recent development, in the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

It has been revealed that there was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k.

It has been revealed that the midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

It has been revealed that this is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

It has been revealed that instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

Recent findings suggest that they are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other massive signings to respond.

It has been revealed that but this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

Erling Haaland gives Manchester City the lead against Liverpool 🎯 https://t.co/cELo5y60Fk.

It has been revealed that in fact, Liverpool’s best performers were the young attackers Victor Muñoz and, making his first league start as a makeshift centre-forward, Lewis Koumas, who is just 21. Against that, City unleashed a battery of forward talent.

"Koumas & Munoz were better than the two £100million players!" Jamie Carragher is still disappointed with what he's seeing from Florian Wirtz in a Liverpool shirt 😬🔴 https://t.co/jJwOZbPJ4b.

Was it an unfair advantage? It appears City have been thriving off that for some time and, while this team were not signed during the years the club have been found guilty of cheating, the argument is, of course, that they would not have joined without the sporting supremacy.

Certainly not Haaland, despite his avowed love for City. That cannot be doubted as his father, Alf-Inge, a former midfielder for the club, stood celebrating in the away end. The striker missed one chance when he should have scored, sent through on goal, shaking his head in disbelief at getting his angles wrong. It felt like a warning and that went unheeded as Doku, who had replaced one of their massive summer signings in Iliman Ndiaye, cut in from the left with his shot deflecting into Haaland’s path. He made no mistake with a powerful, first-time finish.

Doku soon added a second, a sublime strike, as he dribbled goalwards, defenders backing off, and he arced a right-footed shot high beyond Alisson Becker’s grasp.

Industry observers note that "It's a GEM" 💎 A beautiful strike from Jérémy Doku to double Man City's lead! https://t.co/lCUFfQmdLC.

In a recent development, there were delighted chants of “olé” from the City supporters and that arrogance was rewarded by a strutting, emphatic third goal. It was finished by the mercurial Rayan Cherki after he was sent clear by a backheel from Josko Gvardiol, another substitute.

A moment of individual brilliance from Rayan Cherki to put the game beyond all doubt 🤯 https://t.co/wvmTMZcGhW.

It captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. In a sea of uncertainty as to what will now happen, that is something we can be sure of.

It has been revealed that “Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Those signs of defiance were not matched on the pitch. Although it may be a song City will get used to hearing for the rest of this extraordinary, unprecedented campaign.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

Recent findings suggest that “It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”.

Maresca mentioned City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”.

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”.

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

According to recent reports, “The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”.

Industry observers note that the Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

“The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”.

But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission remarked. I think that’s what’s worried me.”.

“The international break is good because we can review what we have done and what we can do better,” Enzo Maresca mentioned after Manchester City’s harum-scarum 5-3 victory over Sunderland. “But at the same time we can relax a little bit more.” One wonders how much respite Enzo Maresca and Manchester City actually enjoyed in the intervening 21 days.

Sources indicate that since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

Arsenal star Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham's record - but a less-familiar name should catch Thomas Tuchel's eye ahead of Euro 2028: THINGS WE LEARNED from England U21's defeat to Portugal

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:46 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.
  • The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:46 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 13 November 2026.

Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.

The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.

But this was to be Dowman's night, smashing the previous record set by Bellingham when he made his England Under-21 debut against Kosovo in 2020 aged 17 years, two months and six days old. Dowman does not turn 17 until December 31.

Under-21s boss Lee Carsley has been keen long before this international break to try to shield Dowman from the weight of expectation.

But on he came, replacing the lively Amario Cozier-Duberry with a smile on his face and a quiet confidence that he didn't take long to show off, bursting past two Portuguese markers before four huddled together to gang up on him.

Breaking records is nothing new to a player that already holds one for being the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer, thanks to his goal against Everton last season.

Max Dowman wrote his name into the record books once more, playing for England Under-21s.

Dowman came on to rich applause on a cold night in Bristol to shatter Jude Bellingham's record.

The Arsenal teenager was lively playing off the right as he now targets the 2027 U21 Euros.

Dowman is both the youngest player to ever win the Premier League and his outing in the Champions League against Slavia Prague last season saw the then-15-year-old become the youngest-ever player to appear in that competition.

By the time next summer's European Championships, which England will attempt to win for a third successive time, rolls around, rising star Dowman could well have earned the right to be this team's main man.

'We've only got three games left before the Euros [next summer],' Carsley explained.

'So it's vital that he puts himself in the shop window to be on the plane.

'It's key that he keeps playing well, getting minutes, showing a really good attitude, like he has done.

According to recent reports, 'I thought he was outstanding when he came on tonight. I thought all of the subs made a real impact.

Sources indicate that 'I thought Max was unlucky not to get an assist... he made a great pass to Mikey Moore.

'He took up some really good positions, both in the 10 and out wide, he's got a significant future ahead.'.

His immense talent was one reason why Arsenal sent Ethan Nwaneri, who Dowman played alongside for part of his cameo, to Marseille on loan, and then similarly to Borussia Dortmund, eager not to block the 16-year-old's pathway.

Carsley knows the diamond he has on his hands and will want to take great care in helping polish a player that this crowd, this England team and this management group know has genuine world class potential.

Speaking of Nwaneri, this felt like a big camp for him. A big camp in the sense that he's falling down the pecking order at Dortmund and is back with a manager that has been so vital in his development.

Nwaneri was part of that 2025 group that won the Euros in front of Thomas Tuchel and he'll have seen the likes of Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott kick on to get to the seniors.

As previously mentioned, Nwaneri was moved out of the way by Arsenal to aid Dowman's development, not an easy pill for a player as talented as he is to stomach when his own development journey is at such a critical juncture given he is, to the surprise of many, still only 19.

'I think we have to remember his age as well,' Carsley added when asked about Nwaneri by Daily Mail Sport.

'He's very young is Ethan and he's another one that we've got a lot of hope for. He's got a lot of potential.'.

Ethan Nwaneri was pushed to the side at Arsenal to benefit Dowman but England is different.

Lee Carsley has been a crucial figure in the development of Nwaneri and this camp was timely.

It was telling that even when Dowman came on, even with the groundswell of excitement at his introduction, it was Carsley's call to keep Nwaneri in his preferred No 10 position with Dowman slotting in on the right.

Nwaneri has only started four games on loan at Dortmund this season and has not managed a single start in the Champions League.

His close control, his quick burst over five yards and the fluidity of his movement was a timely reminder that yes, Dowman is the rising star everyone came out to see, but Nwaneri won't get pushed to the side again without a fight.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is a name not all will be familiar with but come next summer, with the Euros in his sights and promotion to the Premier League on the agenda with Middlesbrough, that could all be about to change.

The 21-year-old has had to be very patient, waiting until last month to make his debut at this level after years of finding himself overlooked.

Here, in what was just his third Under-21 appearance, he revealed over the course of 61 minutes why the days of being looked past should be over.

Sources indicate that one of the big frustrations in the FA right now at Under-21 level is the lack of touchline wingers. Rio Ngumoha, still only 18, has never been capped at the level and has instead been catapulted into the first team, while many, like Ethan Nwaneri, prefer playing inside.

Industry observers note that 'The more we can get our wide players one v one the better,' Carsley said. 'I think sometimes we leave them isolated and the opposition are able to double up on them.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is not a household name at international level but his talent is immense.

'It's crucial that our game strategy can't just be to get the ball wide and hope for the best.'.

Dowman, on in place of Cozier-Duberry is a 10, rather than a right winger which is where he came on, and so a player like Cozier-Duberry, who is on loan at Middlesbrough from Brighton & Hove Albion, is worth his weight in gold.

Here in Bristol he was routinely drawing two defenders and at times three; Portugal knew full well how a quick flip-flap of the ball, or one clipped pass over the top, was enough for the Englishman to take the top off the back-line.

His loan at Bolton Wanderers last season complicated an international journey that has seen him play at Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-19 and Under-20 level, but that's all in the past.

England need a genuine, pacy threat out wide if they are to win a third straight Euros. Cozier-Duberry showed here exactly why he should be it.

EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1176 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation.
  • Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.
  • The European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation. These include a move to ease rules controlling the use of pesticides and herbicides, which help fight pests and weeds.

Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.

The European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default. Safety reviews would only be done in exceptional cases, and regulatory authorities, not the industry, would bear responsibility.

The commission has said its goal is to cut costs, simplify work for authorities and help farmers stay competitive. Scientists and doctors, however, warn that concerns over human health and environmental impact from these toxic substances are being brushed aside.

The European Commission has said it's responding to complaints from farmers and the agriculture industry to clarify EU rules that govern pesticide use.

A joint statement released in May by 19 food associations, including CropLife Europe, which promotes pesticides, said complicated administrative procedures and a lengthy approvals process meant farmers were "left without any effective solutions to protect their crops against insects, weeds and diseases," putting food security and livelihoods at risk.

"The existing system of periodic renewal assessment of every active substance has become unsustainable," the commission's press service told DW, citing "chronic delays" and "bottlenecks" in the approval of fresh, more sustainable products.

In recent negotiations, EU member states stated open-ended authorizations should be restricted to "low-risk active substances.".

But their stance is still wanting to extend initial approval periods for other substances to up to 15 years, and a maximum of 25 years for renewals.

In a recent development, herbert Dorfmann, a center-right Italian member of the European Parliament, said there is right now a yearslong delay in approving new pesticides, including more eco-friendly options, meaning farmers are forced to rely on older substances. Or, if these are banned, go without altogether.

The commission wants to "make the system more efficient and responsive," while guaranteeing that "the protection of human and animal health and the environment remain the highest priorities.".

Dorfmann, who as co-rapporteur is responsible for interinstitutional negotiations on the issue, backs the commission's stance, saying the EU needs "to open up the system for innovation.".

He aims to bring the parliament's proposal on the upcoming pesticide rules to a vote among EU lawmakers before the end of the year.

Ecologists and medical experts, however, have spoken out forcefully against the proposed changes, saying the potential implications for human health and the environment are being downplayed.

In September, more than 500 experts from across the EU signed an open letter calling on the European Parliament to suspend its consideration of the latest regulations and conduct an independent investigation into health and environmental impacts.

On October 7, UN rights experts also backed the call for a full review into whether the proposed changes violated the EU's obligations under international human rights law, especially with regard to agricultural workers and children.

It has been revealed that pesticides can persist in the environment, contaminating water and degrading soils. They can also drive biodiversity loss and poison other animals higher up the food chain.

When it comes to humans, the European Environment Agency has stated it was "not yet possible to estimate the burden of disease linked to current levels of exposure to all pesticides.".

However, exposure to chemical pesticides, including banned substances that still persist in the environment, has been linked to various cancers, chronic respiratory disease, neurological disorders and developmental delays, as well as problems with fertility and behavior.

And exposure is widespread: A survey conducted between 2014 and 2021 found that 84% of urine samples from both children and adults in five European countries contained residue from two or more pesticides.

Martina Vijver, scientific director and ecotoxicology expert at Leiden University in the Netherlands, said experts were "deeply concerned" that the EU's current plan "will weaken rather than strengthen the level of protection for pesticide regulation.".

Speaking at the European Parliament in September, she said regular reassessments were key to evaluating the safety of pesticides with fresh findings, pointing out that the perception of risk changes over time.

"The regulatory system must remain capable of correcting yesterday's decisions with tomorrow's knowledge," she stated.

Salome Roynel, a policy officer at the Pesticide Action Network Europe, an NGO based in Brussels, mentioned the harmful effects of pesticides aren't often fully understood until years later, when the product is up for reconsideration.

"Newly introduced science emerges all the time," she told DW, highlighting how 56 active substances have been banned in the EU since 2011 as a result of periodic reviews.

That includes the insecticide chlorpyrifos, previously used in orchards and on vegetable and cereal crops, which has been tied to harmful effects on children's brain development.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel said it was "obvious that there was some kind of alignment" between the changes proposed by the EU institutions and the demands of the pesticide lobby.

This echoes a new report by nonprofit research and campaign group Corporate Europe Observatory, which noted Dorfmann and other lawmakers had "copy-pasted […] industry demands" into their regulatory proposals.

Dorfmann denied the lobby influence, telling DW he had met with "both sides, industry and environmental associations," in public debates on the issue.

Sources indicate that "The main objective is not to keep old products in the market. The main objective is to bring newly introduced ones to the market," Dorfmann stated.

Part of that blueprint, he added, would be to help more environmentally friendly "biocontrol" products and low-risk substances to bypass current administrative hurdles and get on the market faster.

It's an idea previously championed by Vijver, who agrees that the current system means more environmentally friendly pesticides are stuck in an administrative "traffic jam." She told DW that biocontrol products could go in a green "bus lane" to ease the way to approval at the European Food Safety Authority, while maintaining crucial safety reviews to filter out the more dangerous products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel also supports the strategy to speed up approval for biocontrol substances, but stated it needs to be part of a wider system change that includes financial support, monitoring and training to use these new products, as well as maintaining the restrictions on more harmful chemical pesticides ― not further deregulation.

According to recent reports, "If farmers get easier access to synthetic pesticides tomorrow, they would have no incentive to switch to biocontrol," she said. "It's important to put [biocontrol pesticides] on the market and we fully support that, but… it will not be the silver bullet.".

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 17:30, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 17:33.

Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe were reportedly both initially considered by Manchester United as potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but the club ultimately went in a different direction.

Mauricio Pochettino will officially begin work as Man United head coach on Thursday, with the Argentine agreeing to replace Carrick at Old Trafford.

Carrick was sacked by the 20-time English champions last week due to the team's struggles in the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign.

Conte and Howe have both been heavily linked with the role in recent weeks; the former is available immediately following his exit from Napoli at the end of last season, while the latter departed Newcastle United ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League campaign.

According to The Athletic, Man United's minority shareholder Sir Jim Ratcliffe had been keen on exploring a move for Conte given his credentials.

The report claims that Conte was interested in the position at Old Trafford, with representatives contacting Man United to make that point clear.

However, some senior figures at Old Trafford did not believe that Conte was the right fit at this moment in time, with the club going through a difficult period.

The 57-year-old was in charge of Chelsea between July 2016 and July 2018, winning the Premier League title and FA Cup at Stamford Bridge, and he then managed Tottenham Hotspur between November 2021 and March 2023.

As a result, a move to Man United would have equalled a third spell in the Premier League.

Howe, meanwhile, has taken charge of Bournemouth, Burnley and Newcastle United during his management career, and his vast experience in the Premier League placed him in the running.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox is believed to have pushed Howe's name into the conversation, but 'the matter did not progress further', while it is understood that the 48-year-old was 'left off the final names considered'.

The Athletic insist that a move to Man United for Howe was never at an advanced stage despite the recent reports.

Former France manager Didier Deschamps was allegedly contacted over the position, but discussions with the Frenchman's representatives are not believed to have been positive.

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 17:43.

Liverpool would reportedly love to sign Ronald Araujo permanently from Barcelona following a series of impressive performances since his arrival at Anfield.

Araujo joined the Reds on loan from La Liga giants Barcelona, with the Merseyside club holding an option to make his move permanent for £47m.

The Uruguay international had struggled during the past couple of seasons at the Catalan club, making the switch a potentially beneficial move for all parties involved.

So far, the 27-year-old defender has proved to be an excellent addition, making 10 Premier League appearances and starting eight of them.

It has previously been reported that the Reds are considering signing Araujo permanently following his impressive start to life at Anfield.

With Conor Bradley sidelined, Araujo has done an excellent job filling the void at right-back, while he has also featured as a centre-back under Andoni Iraola.

According to Marca, Liverpool would happily make his move permanent right now, but they can only activate the option at the end of the season.

Araujo is mentioned to be happy at Liverpool, but the Reds are taking a cautious approach to the defender's situation in case he suffers an injury or experiences a significant dip in form.

Liverpool will need to recruit a latest centre-back, and potentially another right-back, next season, making Araujo an appealing option.

Having spent an entire season working under Iraola, the defender should also have a much better understanding of the manager's tactical demands.

At the same time, much will depend on where Liverpool finish the campaign and whether their final league position influences their transfer aims.

Araujo still has several good years of football ahead of him, but the Reds may be tempted to invest the money in promising young talent or use it to bring Jarell Quansah back to Anfield.

#25654. What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
